title: Briefing: Germany, Albania, Italy, India, Serbia and France
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Monday, November second. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means only one source has it so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.

Germany. Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien calls the concerns of the young people who marched in more than 30 cities on October thirty-first "legitimate and extremely relevant" and promises more dialogue, and SPD politicians call for a national education summit. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, The Local Germany, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

Albania. Tirana Mayor Erion Veliaj, held in pre-trial detention on corruption charges he denies, accused Prime Minister Edi Rama of orchestrating his Oct 28 transfer to Fier prison and of using Justice Minister Toni Gogu to demand he give up control of the city, Tirana Times reports. We grade that disputed: the accounts conflict, and our timeline sets out both.

Italy. The education branch of the CGIL union says it will join the CGIL general strike on November twentieth, citing budget-law cuts of 4,925 teaching posts and 2,049 support staff from 2027/28 and no funds for the contract renewal, Scuola Mag reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Scuola Mag, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

India. Thousands march in New Delhi to Ramlila Maidan in a Congress-led opposition rally, headed by Rahul Gandhi, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over a voter-list revision that removed more than 130 million names, Al Jazeera and Reuters report. We grade that reported: so far only Al Jazeera has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

Serbia. Thousands mark two years since the Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse that killed 16 people, with a silent march in the rain, 16 wreaths and 16 minutes of silence, AP and AFP report. Our grade: confirmed, with independent reporting from AP and Malay Mail.

France. From October thirty-first: More than 300,000 people join a new wave of protests on Saturday, smaller than the mid-October unrest, Bloomberg reports; in Paris, where about 70,000 officers were deployed, police arrest 779 people and five officers are injured. We grade that reported: so far only Bloomberg has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.
On the stories with no new developments in the last three days, here are the latest reports.

Canada. No new developments since October thirtieth. The latest report: Tsartlip First Nation, on Vancouver Island, files for judicial review in the Federal Court of the Pacific Link national-interest designation, saying federal consultation was rushed and ignored its treaty rights, CTV News reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, CTV News, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

South Africa. No new developments since October thirtieth. The latest report: A Durban court lets the anti-migrant group March and March keep demonstrating but only between 9am and 3pm, without weapons or face coverings and without damaging property, AFP reports. We grade that reported: so far only 24 News HD has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.
We'll bring you updates on those as soon as they become available.
Germany's Gen Z protests. Coming up: Gen Z regelt plans another countrywide protest on November fourteenth.

Serbia's student movement. Prosecutors order the 48-hour detention of Marko Kričak, head of the criminal police, and another senior officer on suspicion of abuse of office linked to a murder investigation, AP reports. Our grade: alleged. That's a claim by one side that no one has independently confirmed. Coming up: Formation of the new government and the choice of prime minister.

France's high school protests. From October thirty-first: Student unions call for school blockades this week and urge students to join the cross-sector strike on November fifth, Bloomberg reports. We grade that reported: so far only Bloomberg has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.
Coming up in the days ahead. November fourth, South Africa: Local government elections on November fourth.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
